payload.title: CUTLASS Tile Scheduling
payload.summary: CUTLASS 3.x provides multiple tile scheduling strategies that control how persistent kernels assign output tiles to thread blocks. This document covers Persistent Scheduler, Stream-K work stealing, Grouped GEMM scheduling, Dependent Kernel Launch (PDL), tile heuristics, and SM90/SM100/SM120 scheduler differences.

sections.heading: Tile Scheduler Overview
sections.gist: All CUTLASS 3.x GEMM kernels are persistent kernels -- thread blocks run continuously throughout the kernel's lifetimeuru, fetching the next tile to compute from the tile scheduler.

sections.heading: Persistent Tile Scheduler
sections.gist: The Persistent scheduler is CUTLASS's default tile scheduling strategy.

sections.heading: Stream-K Work Stealing
sections.gist: Stream-K is a fine-grained work decomposition strategy that splits GEMM along the K dimension, so that a single "work unit" can span partial K intervals across multiple output tiles.

sections.heading: Grouped GEMM Scheduler
sections.gist: Grouped kernels execute multiple independent GEMM problems in a single CUDA launch, processing them sequentially through a persistent loop.

sections.heading: Dependent Kernel Launch (PDL)
sections.gist: PDL allows two adjacent kernels in the same CUDA stream to overlap in execution.

sections.heading: Tile Heuristics
sections.gist: CUTLASS provides analytical heuristic tools `nvidia-matmul-heuristics` to assist in selecting kernel configurations.
